examples.text: 보다 보면 재미가 있겠지, 승찬이가 지금은 경험이 부족해서 그렇지.
examples.trans: Keep watching and it will get funny—Seung-chan just lacks experience for now.
This expression comes from 'because it is lacking'.

meanings.en: a lot, much, in large quantity
meanings.note: Adverbial form of 많다 (to be many/much)

examples.trans: I did a lot of work today.

I was busy today because of itself.

examples.trans: Most loved? I like that line just now, since it is true! Still, these script lines sound way too pitiful for someone so loved.

examples.trans: Oh no, sir—not at all!
Here the word for 'how could that possibly be!' is key.
Let's I think together today.
I worked hard to I think yesterday too.

examples.text: 자신의 옆을 지켜주고 이해해 줄 어떤 존재를 바라고 계신 것 같습니다.
examples.trans: It seems you are hoping for someone who will stay by your side and understand you.

examples.text: 신디야, 엄마가 너 그렇게 가르쳤니? 그렇게 온몸에 힘을 다 주고 얘기를 하면 들키잖아, 네가 지금 자신이 없다는 거.
examples.trans: Cindy, did Mom teach you to negotiate like that? When you tense up your whole body while talking, it gives away that you lack confidence right now.

괜찮다.gloss: to be fine; to be okay

meanings.en: to be fine; to be okay; to be alright
meanings.note: Used to reassure someone, decline an offer politely, or say something is acceptable.

examples.trans: I'm really fine.
Is it okay if we meet tomorrow?

meanings.note: noun eye

examples.trans: Eye hurts.
Eyes are big.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (adj).

examples.text: 통계상 시즌 첫 방송은 전 시즌 마지막 방송보다 2 정도 높았더라고요.
examples.trans: Statistically, a season premiere rated about two points higher than the previous finale.
This expression comes from 'was higher, I found'.

meanings.note: Usually followed by a negative verb to mean 'nobody' or 'nothing'.

examples.trans: Nobody is here.
Please give me anything.

examples.text: 나도 알지, 우리가 너무 오래 붙어 있었다는 거. 그래서 내가 이런 말 한 건 이십오 년 우리 우정을 건 도박 같은 거라는 것도.
examples.trans: I know too that we have been stuck together far too long—and that saying what I said was a gamble staking our twenty-five-year friendship.

examples.text: 야, 나 눈 높아! 아무나 이십오 년씩 만나고 안 그래.
examples.trans: Hey, I have high standards! I do not stay friends with just anyone for twenty-five years.

examples.text: 나 십 년 동안 시키는 대로 다 했잖아요.
examples.trans: For ten years, I did everything you told me to do.

examples.text: 이십 년 넘게 친구 설정으로 지냈는데 쉽진 않겠지.
examples.trans: You lived as friends for over twenty years, so changing that won't be easy.

meanings.note: Action of coming together with someone.

examples.trans: I meet a friend.
Let's meet tomorrow.

meanings.note: Interrogative pronoun for location.

examples.trans: Where is the restroom?
Where are you right now?

examples.trans: Ah, yes.
Yes, I understand.

meanings.note: commonly used with -에 (옆에)

examples.trans: Please sit next to me.
There is a cafe next to the bank.

meanings.note: Used as past adnominal (변한).

examples.text: 그러게요, 이제 보고 싶은 엄마도 없고 가고 싶은 집도 없고 나 참 많이 변한 것 같아요.
examples.trans: Indeed—now I have no mother I long to see and no home I want to return to; I really have changed a lot.
Let us do that (have changed) right away.

않다.gloss: to not do, to not be

meanings.en: to not do, to not be
meanings.note: Auxiliary negative verb/adjective used after -지 (long-form negation)

examples.trans: The weather isn't cold today.
I didn't say anything.

meanings.en: actually, in fact, to tell the truth
meanings.note: adverbial use of the noun 사실 (fact)

examples.trans: Honestly, I don't know well either.
In fact, I couldn't sleep yesterday.

meanings.note: Used as causal -어서 (까먹어서…).

examples.text: 죄송합니다, 요거는 제가 아까 먼저 까먹어서…
examples.trans: I am sorry—I already ate mine first earlier…
Let us do that (already gobbled up, so…) right away.

meanings.note: Auxiliary verb used after -지 to tell someone not to do something. Ending with -고 (말고) gives a brisk, trailing command. RR: malda.

examples.trans: Please do not worry.
Do not be late, and come early.

meanings.note: Used when repeating an action.

examples.trans: See you again!
It is raining again.
